title: 07-Ghost
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Teito Klein, a former slave and orphan, is a top student at the Barsburg Empire's military academy until an overheard state secret awakens memories that he is heir to a conquered kingdom. He flees to a church sanctuary, where priests including the lecherous Frau shelter him, while the empire, and the officer Ayanami, pursue him and his best friend Mikage is sacrificed (Viz blurb via MU; AniList; ANN review of volume 1).
life_message: Loyalty, friendship and faith can sustain someone through loss and a past that others tried to erase.

content.note: War, slavery and deaths of people close to Teito, including his best friend (ANN; AniList War, Slavery, Tragedy); MU Brutality, Genocide, Child Abuse.
Gloomy, angsty tone (ANN); demons, possession and deals with the devil (MU; AniList Demons).
Homoerotic subtext and bishonen fan service, lecherous priest (ANN); MU BL Subtext.
Trauma, memory manipulation, mockery as an orphan and slave (ANN; MU Traumatized Male Lead).

dominant: Invented church mythology of good and evil; resistance to an imperial military; found family and loyalty

frames.aligns: Church as sanctuary; friendship unto death; evil of slavery.
frames.concerns: Invented deity looks like a grim reaper; priests caricatured; demonic pacts.

frames.aligns: Struggle of light and darkness; self-sacrifice.

frames.concerns: Fictional god, exorcism and possession; homoerotic subtext.
Demons, deals with the devil and possession treated as fantasy.
Depicted deity (second commandment concern); lecherous priest.

frames.aligns: Fantasy framing of good and evil in a Lewis-like mode.
Reincarnation and dharma of a rightful heir.
Loyalty, duty, a rightful heir restored.

frames.concerns: Spirits, ghosts and possession shown as real.
Spiritism, demons, violence and invented worship.

folkways.japan: Uses European church and empire imagery filtered through Japanese fantasy, common in josei and shoujo-adjacent works.

delivery.evidence: ANN describes a mythology of good and evil, no stated message (to verify).
delivery.note: The good-versus-evil mythology is carried by plot; no source reports characters voicing ideologies.

winners_losers: Teito and the church allies get the sympathy; the Barsburg Empire and its military are cast as oppressors (ANN; Viz blurb).
to_verify: ANN review covers only volume 1 (Go! Comi edition).
